msItem.title: Sacramentarium (frgm.)
msItem.note: The dating of the manuscript revised from that in the second edition of Medieval Libraries of Great Britain (1964) fits the fact that the main body of the sacramentary includes borrowings from the Romano-Germanic Pontifical. [This note was added in MLGB3, a project that was predominantly active between 2010-2015; however, at least parts of this record were evidently updated in 2016 or later].

provenance.orgName: Winchester, Hampshire. Benedictine cathedral priory of St Peter, St Paul, and St Swithun
provenance.p: This attribution was accepted in the second edition of Medieval Libraries of Great Britain (1964), which did not change in the Supplement. However, there were relevant changes during MLGB3 (see note on date above). Specifically, a query was added to the attribution, along with the following note:

p.q: Saints culted at both Old and New Minsters are in the text, but the provision of an 'Oratio in noui monasterii ecclesia' would suggest the New Minster. The immediately preceding entry, with prayer addressed to the Virgin and all her virgins, probably relates to the new tower of the New Minster that was erected in the 980s, probably at the north-west end of the building, and which included at ground level a porticus dedicated to the Virgin. The processional route that is here outlined seems to be from the Old Minster to the church of St Gregory (at the south-west corner of New Minster), the procession then moving from the porticus chapel of St Mary into the main body of the New Minster. (This pers. comm. from Derek Keene, 2016; discussion to appear in the Historic Town Atlas volume on Winchester, and text and discussion to appear in Winchester Studies vol. 4/1.).

provenance.orgName: Hyde (Hida, formerly New Minster, Winchester), Hampshire, Benedictine abbey of Holy Trinity, St Mary the Virgin, and St Peter
provenance.p: This attribution was rejected in the second edition of Medieval Libraries of Great Britain (1964), though the corresponding dagger was inadvertently omitted in the index (see pp. 104, 394). There were no relevant changes in the Supplement (1987). The corresponding Medieval Libraries of Great Britain index card records the following information, which (originally) was deemed unsatisfactory for an attribution: The Newminster Missal. Contains an oratio in noui monasterii ecclesia, invoking St Peter, Paul, Judoc, and Grimbald. This evidence was evidently reconsidered in MLGB3 (2010-2015), as seen above from the notes under Winchester Benedictine Cathedral priory. With this in mind, the attribution has now (i.e. in 2026) been changed from rejected to accepted (with a query).

history.provenance: John More monk (fol. i, s. xvi).

recordHist.source: Neil R. Ker, ed., Medieval Libraries of Great Britain: A List of Surviving Books, Royal Historical Society Guides and Handbooks, 3 (London, 1941; 2nd edn, 1964; supplement, ed. Andrew G. Watson, 1987; digital edn, ed. Richard Sharpe and James M. W. Willoughby, 2010–15).

revisionDesc.change: Record edited (Sian Witherden) to clarify data history and to incorporate Hyde attribution. As outlined in the record, the Hyde attribution was once rejected, but has here been accepted with a query in line with the rest of the pre-existing MLGB3 record).
